clause_title: Constitutional Authority & Five-Tier Financial Delegation
clause_text: 1.1 Framed under Section 179 of the Companies Act, 2013 and Maharatna CPSE autonomy guidelines, the Board of Directors of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) delegates financial and commercial sanction powers across five executive levels: Level 1 Board Finance Committee / Full Board; Level 2 Chairman (CMD); Level 3 Executive Committee (CMD + Whole-Time Functional Directors); Level 4 Whole-Time Functional Directors (Director Finance, Director Refineries, Director Marketing, Director Pipelines, Director BD); Level 5 Executive Directors / Refinery Unit Heads / Grade D-H Functional Heads. 1.2 Powers attach strictly to posts within approved Capital/Operating budgets.

clause_title: Spot & Term Crude Oil Cargo Procurement Thresholds
clause_text: 2.1 Crude oil cargo procurement through Empowered Standing Committee (Crude Import Cell — Refineries & International Trade) is governed by volume-value tiers: (a) Up to Rs 2,500 Cr per VLCC / Aframax spot cargo tender within approved monthly crude LP basket: Executive Director (International Trade) with Associate Finance concurrence; (b) Rs 2,500 Cr to Rs 5,000 Cr or non-standard opportunity high-TAN / sour crude trials: Joint sanction by Director (Refineries) and Director (Finance); (c) Term crude supply contracts exceeding Rs 5,000 Cr annual commitment or Sovereign G2G term renewals: Executive Committee / Chairman with post-facto reporting to the Board of Directors.

clause_title: VLCC & Coastal Shipping Chartering Delegation
clause_text: 2.2 Spot voyage charters and coastal product tanker fixtures on Worldscale benchmarks: up to Rs 75 Cr per charter party by ED (Shipping/Logistics) with Finance concurrence; Rs 75 Cr to Rs 250 Cr by Director (Refineries) + Director (Finance); multi-year time-charter Ind AS 116 vessel leases exceeding Rs 250 Cr NPV require Executive Committee / Board approval.

clause_title: Refinery Turnaround (M&I) & Maintenance Capex Sanction
clause_text: 3.1 Planned Refinery Maintenance & Inspection (M&I) Shutdown / Turnaround packages (FCCU, Hydrocracker, DCU catalyst replacements and furnace retubing): (a) Refinery Unit Head (ED/CGM) up to Rs 50 Cr per package under advertised tender; (b) Director (Refineries) with Director (Finance) concurrence up to Rs 200 Cr; (c) Turnaround packages Rs 200 Cr to Rs 500 Cr: Executive Committee; (d) Above Rs 500 Cr: Board of Directors / Board Finance Committee.

clause_title: Maharatna Capital Project & Joint Venture Investment Limits
clause_text: 3.2 Under DPE Maharatna Financial Autonomy guidelines, IOCL Board is empowered to approve brownfield refinery expansions (such as Panipat P-25, Koyali, Barauni), cross-country pipelines, petrochemical complexes, and JV/subsidiary equity commitments up to Rs 5,000 Cr per project (or 15% of Net Worth capped at Rs 5,000 Cr for a single subsidiary/JV without Cabinet/MoPNG reference), subject to mandatory appraisal by the Board Finance & Investment Committee.

clause_title: Whole-Time Functional Directors & Chairman Emergency Powers
clause_text: 4.1 Whole-Time Directors (Director Finance, Director Refineries, Director Marketing) exercise independent revenue and non-plan capital sanction up to Rs 150 Cr per contract with Finance concurrence. 4.2 Chairman (CMD) exercises sanctioning authority up to Rs 350 Cr, and up to Rs 500 Cr in documented refinery safety, pipeline integrity, or national fuel supply continuity emergencies, subject to reporting at the immediately succeeding Board meeting.

clause_title: Three-Tier Finance Concurrence & Prohibition of Split Tendering
clause_text: 5.1 Every procurement or capital commitment above Rs 10 Lakh requires sequential: (i) Administrative Approval, (ii) Technical Sanction, and (iii) Associate Finance Concurrence certifying budget availability and commercial parity. 5.2 Splitting work orders, crude parcels, or EPC packages to stay below a higher approval tier (e.g., splitting a Rs 220 Cr turnaround into four Rs 55 Cr contracts) is strictly prohibited and treated as audit non-compliance.

clause_title: Board Finance & Audit Committee Reserved Approvals
clause_text: 6.1 Reserved exclusively for the Board / Finance Committee: (a) Annual Capital & Revenue Budgets (BE/RE); (b) Long-term NCD issuances, ECB loans, and commercial borrowing programs exceeding Rs 2,500 Cr per tranche; (c) Quarterly & Annual audited financial statements and interim/final dividend declarations; (d) Strategic M&A, subsidiary capitalization (CPCL, Lanka IOC), and impairment testing under Ind AS 36.

clause_title: Single / Proprietary OEM Catalyst & Licensor Sanctions
clause_text: 7.1 Procurement of proprietary refinery hydrocracker/FCC catalysts, process unit licensor packages (UOP, Axens, Haldor Topsoe), and OEM compressor spares on Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) requires Finance Director concurrence above Rs 25 Cr and Executive Committee ratification above Rs 75 Cr.

clause_title: Confidentiality of Unpublished Board Packs, Tender Bids & Sub-Ledgers
clause_text: 8.1 Unpublished Board Finance Committee draft agenda packs, Q1/quarterly pre-release refinery margin sub-ledgers, live crude tender bid tabulations, and counterparty commercial pricing discounts are classified CONFIDENTIAL under IOCL Information Security & SEBI PIT Regulations. Access is restricted strictly to Chairman, Whole-Time Directors, and authorized Board Secretariat / Treasury Officers; Grade A-D officers must submit formal Access Requests approved by Director (Finance).

clause_title: Objectives & Commodity Risk Governance Structure
clause_text: 1.1 The IOCL Commodity & Forex Risk Management Policy establishes disciplined hedging guardrails to protect Core GRM, mitigate NRV inventory write-downs, and stabilize USD/INR debt servicing. 1.2 Overseen by the Board Risk Management Committee (RMC) and executed jointly by the Executive Risk Committee (Director Finance + Director Refineries + ED Treasury).

clause_title: Unpriced Crude Cargo-in-Transit Exposure Window
clause_text: 2.1 IOCL faces ~38-45 days of pricing mismatch between crude Bill-of-Lading loading and Indian coastal refinery intake. 2.2 The Treasury Commodity Desk is authorized to hedge 25% to 50% of net unpriced Brent/Dubai cargo-in-transit volumes via OTC ICE Brent swaps and zero-cost put-spread collars with tenors up to 90 days.

clause_title: Refining Crack-Spread Hedging Band (Gasoil, ATF & Gasoline)
clause_text: 3.1 To lock cyclical refining margins when Singapore Gasoil 10ppm or Jet/Kero regrade spreads exceed 1-sigma historical thresholds, IOCL may hedge 25% to 35% of rolling 6-month discretionary exportable distillate surplus (Gasoil/ATF/MS Singapore swaps) up to a rolling 12-month horizon with Director (Finance) and Director (Refineries) sign-off.

clause_title: Inventory Price Protection & Core Operational Buffer Policy
clause_text: 4.1 Core minimum operating stock (~35 MMT pipeline/tank bottoms) is unhedged long-term capital, whereas discretionary seasonal inventory builds above norm (DIO > 55 days) require dynamic delta-protection put spreads whenever Brent backwardation flips to contango or volatility exceeds 35% annualized, guarding against FY20-style NRV write-downs.

clause_title: USD/INR Foreign Currency Debt & Import Bill Forward Cover
clause_text: 5.1 IOCL maintains a rolling 50% to 75% hedge ratio on short-term (< 6 month) USD Letters of Credit / Buyer's Credit and crude import payables via deliverable forwards and seagull option structures. 5.2 Long-term ECBs and USD bonds shall maintain minimum 50% principal + coupon hedge via Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) unless matched against natural USD export/ATF/international subsidiary inflows.

clause_title: Strict Prohibition on Speculative / Naked Derivatives
clause_text: 6.1 Under RBI FEMA guidelines and IOCL Board mandate, all commodity and FX derivatives must map 1:1 to underlying physical crude cargoes, refined product cracks, or foreign currency liabilities. Selling uncovered naked calls, leveraged exotic knock-in structures, or net-long speculative positions exceeding underlying exposure is strictly barred.

clause_title: ISDA Counterparty Credit Exposure Ceilings (Confidential Named Limits)
clause_text: 7.1 Derivative trades may be executed only with RBI Category-I Authorised Dealer banks and clearing houses rated AA-/A1+ or higher under executed ISDA Master Agreements. Single-counterparty Mark-to-Market exposure limits and bank-wise credit utilization matrices are confidential treasury controls restricted to CMD, Director (Finance), and Grade C+ Treasury leads.

clause_title: Ind AS 109 Hedge Accounting & Quarterly MTM Reporting
clause_text: 8.1 Hedge effectiveness is tested quarterly under Ind AS 109 (80%-125% dollar-offset / regression corridor); effective cash-flow hedge gains/losses route through Other Comprehensive Income (OCI) Cash Flow Hedge Reserve until inventory recognition, while ineffective portions and unhedged FX restatements flow to Note 33 / Finance Costs.

clause_title: Ind AS 115 Revenue Recognition: Gross Turnover vs Central Excise Duty
clause_text: Per IOCL Annual Report Significant Accounting Policies & Note 28, Revenue from Operations is recognized at fair value upon transfer of control of petroleum products, petrochemicals, and natural gas. Because Central Excise Duty is an indirect levy collected by IOCL as principal manufacturer/refiner, Gross Revenue from Operations includes Central Excise Duty (Rs 1,02,066.54 Cr in FY26 out of Rs 8,86,224.41 Cr Gross Revenue), and Excise Duty is presented as a separate expense line on the face of Statement of Profit & Loss, yielding Net Revenue of Rs 7,84,157.87 Cr.

clause_title: Ind AS 2 Inventories Valuation: Lower of FIFO Cost or NRV
clause_text: Per IOCL Annual Report Note 11, Raw Materials (crude oil) and Finished Petroleum Products are valued at the lower of cost (determined on First-In-First-Out / weighted moving average formula across refineries/depots) and Net Realizable Value (NRV). Sharp Brent price declines trigger NRV write-downs (including Rs 11,305.00 Cr classified as an Exceptional Item in FY20 during Q4 COVID-19 price collapse), explaining gaps between Reported GRM and Core GRM.

clause_title: Ind AS 116 Leases: Coastal Time-Charters, Tank-Trucks & Retail Outlets
clause_text: Effective FY20 (1 April 2019), IOCL adopted Ind AS 116 Leases using modified retrospective approach, recognizing Right-of-Use (ROU) assets inside PPE (Note 2) and corresponding Lease Liabilities (Note 19A: Rs 9,480 Cr non-current in FY26) for coastal oil tankers, tank-truck fleets, LNG/LPG terminals, and retail outlet land sites. Lease expense shifted from operating rentals (Note 33) into DD&A (Note 2) and Finance Costs (Note 34).

clause_title: Ind AS 12 Income Taxes: Section 115BAA (25.168% Regime)
clause_text: In FY20, IOCL exercised the irrevocable option permitted under Section 115BAA of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (enacted via Taxation Laws Amendment Ordinance 2019), reducing its statutory corporate income tax rate to 25.168% (22% base + 10% surcharge + 4% cess) while foregone MAT credits and remeasured deferred tax liabilities yielded an effective FY26 tax rate of 25.13% (Rs 12,351.00 Cr total tax on Rs 49,153.42 Cr PBT).

clause_title: Operating Segment Disclosures: Petroleum Products, Petrochemicals & Others
clause_text: Per IOCL Annual Report Segment Reporting under Ind AS 108, IOCL reports three operating segments to the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CMD & Functional Directors): (1) Sale of Petroleum Products (refining + marketing wholesale/retail), (2) Sale of Petrochemicals (Panipat cracker, PX/PTA, Gujarat polymer units), and (3) Other Business Activities (gas marketing, pipelines services, E&P/upstream & green energy). Unallocable corporate borrowings and interest sit in corporate pool.

clause_title: Ind AS 110 / 28 Consolidation: Standalone vs IOC.NS Group Entities
clause_text: Consolidated Financial Statements (IOC.NS) aggregate IOCL Standalone (PAT Rs 36,802.42 Cr in FY26) with controlled subsidiaries — notably Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL, 51.89%), Lanka IOC PLC (75.12%), IOC Middle East FZE (100%), and IndOil Global B.V. (100%) — plus equity-accounted Joint Ventures including Hindustan Urvarak & Rasayan (HURL, 29.67%) and Petronet LNG (12.50%), arriving at FY26 Consolidated PAT of Rs 39,639.54 Cr after inter-company eliminations.

clause_title: Indane LPG Consumer Security Deposits & Government LPG Buffer/Grants
clause_text: IOCL recognizes refundable security deposits received from domestic Indane LPG consumers against cylinders and pressure regulators under Other Financial Liabilities (exceeding Rs 34,000 Cr float). Government compensation for under-recoveries on domestic LPG (such as the Rs 10,801.00 Cr one-time grant in FY23) is recognized in Revenue from Operations under Ind AS 20 upon sanction order confirmation from MoPNG.

clause_title: Ind AS 16 Useful Lives: Refineries (25 yrs), Pipelines (30 yrs) & Tanks
clause_text: Property, Plant & Equipment (Net Block Rs 2,16,840.00 Cr in FY26) is depreciated on straight-line method over Schedule II / technical assessed useful lives: Refinery Process Plants & Catalysts (15-25 years), Cross-Country Pipelines (30 years), Storage Tanks & Railway Sidings (15-30 years), and Retail Outlet Dispensing Assets (15 years). Major turnaround inspection costs are capitalized and amortized over the 3-4 year statutory turnaround cycle.

clause_title: Stage-Gate Capex Appraisal & 12% Post-Tax Equity IRR Hurdle Rate
clause_text: 1.1 All new discretionary capital expenditure proposals above Rs 100 Cr must clear Stage-Gate Gate-2 (DPR feasibility) and Gate-3 (Investment Sanction) demonstrating a minimum Post-Tax Equity IRR of >= 12.0% (or >= WACC + 250 bps) under conservative base-case crack and margin assumptions, verified independently by Corporate Finance Appraisal Group.

clause_title: Brownfield Refinery & Petchem Expansion Priority Queue
clause_text: 2.1 Priority capital budget allocation targets high-return brownfield refining capacity and petrochemical integration lowering import dependence: Panipat P-25 (15 -> 25 MMTPA + PX/PTA), Gujarat Koyali (13.7 -> 18 MMTPA), Barauni (6 -> 9 MMTPA), and Paradip product pipeline spurs. Projects experiencing > 15% cost escalation or > 6 months CWIP slippage trigger mandatory Director (Finance) & Board Audit re-appraisal.

clause_title: DIPAM Dividend Payout Policy (30%-40% PAT / 5% Net Worth)
clause_text: 3.1 In alignment with DIPAM CPSE Capital Restructuring Guidelines, IOCL targets an annual dividend payout of 30%-40% of Standalone Profit After Tax (or 5% of Net Worth, whichever is higher), balanced against debt-reduction milestones and peak brownfield Capex outflows (e.g., FY26 DPS Rs 8.50/share = Rs 12,003.05 Cr = 32.6% payout).

clause_title: Target Capital Structure Guardrail (D/E <= 0.70x & AAA Rating)
clause_text: 4.1 IOCL maintains a through-cycle Debt-to-Equity guardrail of <= 0.70x (with strategic target <= 0.55x during normal refining margins, achieved at 0.54x in FY26) and Net Debt / EBITDA <= 2.0x to safeguard domestic AAA credit ratings and keep pretax borrowing cost competitive below 7.25%.

clause_title: Net-Zero 2046 Green Capex & Renewable Power Wheeling Pool
clause_text: 5.1 IOCL ring-fences 10%-15% of annual capital budget toward Net-Zero Operational Emissions (Scope 1 & 2) by 2046, spanning Panipat Green Hydrogen electrolyzers, 2G/3G ethanol biorefineries, compressed biogas (CBG) plants, EV charging/battery-swapping hubs, and captive solar wheeling targeting 35% green refinery grid share.

clause_title: Working Capital DIO Ceiling (<= 55.6 Days) & OCF Sweep
clause_text: 6.1 Cash released from reducing crude & product inventory days (DIO target <= 55.6 days vs 58.6 days in FY26) and MoPNG LPG buffer reimbursements shall be swept first to retire high-cost short-term Commercial Paper and Working Capital Demand Loans (WCDL) before discretionary treasury deployment.

clause_title: Subsidiary Capital Calls & CPCL / Overseas Upstream Gating
clause_text: 7.1 Any fresh equity infusion or corporate guarantee for CPCL, Lanka IOC, or overseas upstream/petchem JVs requires parent standalone FCF coverage >= 1.2x post-dividend and demonstrated standalone ROCE recovery above 12%.

clause_title: Bonus Share Capitalization & Investor Disclosures
clause_text: 8.1 Bonus capitalizations (historically 1:1 in FY18 and 1:2 in FY23) require Free Reserves / Securities Premium certification by Statutory Auditors and post-bonus EPS/DPS pro-forma adjustment in Investor Relations KPI tables.

clause_title: Maharatna MoU Composite Framework & Weightage Structure
clause_text: 1.1 Annual Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between IOCL and Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG) / Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) assigns 100 composite points across: Financial Parameters (Net Revenue, Operating EBITDA/Net Revenue %, Capex Spend, PAT/Net Worth = 50%), Downstream Operational Efficiency (Refinery Throughput MMT, Distillate Yield, Pipeline Utilization, MBN Energy Index = 30%), and Energy Transition / ESG / Governance (20%).

clause_title: Rating Bands: Excellent (>= 90 Score) vs Very Good (>= 70 Score)
clause_text: 2.1 MoU Excellent rating threshold requires composite score >= 90/100 (or >= 4.00/5.00 normalized index). FY25 composite rating finished 'Very Good' (3.82/5.00) amid compressed diesel cracks, whereas FY26 projected 'Excellent' (4.35/5.00) driven by record 75.451 MMT throughput, Rs 7,84,157.87 Cr Net Revenue, and Rs 34,210 Cr Capex execution.

clause_title: Refinery Specific Energy Consumption (MBN) & Distillate Yield Targets
clause_text: 3.1 MoU operational efficiency KPIs track corporate weighted MBN (Thousand British Thermal Units per Barrel per Energy Factor), Fuel & Loss % (FY26 8.20%, FY27 target <= 7.90%), and Distillate Yield % (FY26 82.8%, FY27 target >= 83.3%) across all 9 standalone refineries.

clause_title: Procurement Compliance: GeM Portal & MSE 25% Sourcing Mandate
clause_text: 4.1 Mandatory DPE MoU compliance tracks procurement of goods and services through Government e-Marketplace (GeM), achieving >= 25% annual procurement from Micro & Small Enterprises (MSEs), and MSME Trade Receivable TReDS settlement within 45 days.

clause_title: Energy Transition Milestones: Biofuels, Ethanol E20 & Green Hydrogen
clause_text: 5.1 MoU ESG KPIs measure Ethanol-Blended Petrol ratio (E15/E20 rollout), Compressed Bio-Gas (SATAT) off-take, Solar photovoltaic installations across retail outlets, and Panipat Green Hydrogen plant commissioning milestones.

clause_title: Quarterly Chairman & Director (Finance) Review & Internal Audit
clause_text: 6.1 Performance against MoU targets is reviewed monthly by Functional Directors and quarterly by Chairman and Audit Committee prior to half-yearly MoPNG / DPE submission, ensuring zero surprise variance at March 31 year-end.
